financials_interim.notes: Company-basis (standalone, ex-Waverly Power subsidiary) column of the same filing. operating_profit derived the same way as the Group row (Gross Profit + Other Operating Income - S&D - Admin = 201,866+17,246-30,000-87,050 = 102,062); ties: 102,062-771=101,291=stated PBT. finance_income/finance_costs split (29,612 / 30,383) taken from the Statement of Cash Flows and nets to exactly (771), matching the P&L's stated Net Finance Cost for the Company column with no gap (unlike the Group column, which had a ~181k unreconciled gap). EPS check: 64,137/500,000,000=0.128 ~= stated 0.13; prior 100,833/500,000,000=0.202 ~= stated 0.20 -- consistent, no swap.

operating_profit is a derived subtotal (Gross Profit + Other Operating Income - Selling & Distribution Expenses - Administrative Expenses = 212,856+15,304-30,000-87,968 = 110,192) since the filing's own P&L jumps straight from Admin Expenses to a single net 'Net Finance Income/(Cost)' line and then PBT, with no operating-profit subtotal presented; verified it ties: 110,192 - 774 = 109,418 = stated PBT (and for the prior year 120,835 - 6,704 = 114,131 = stated prior PBT). finance_income/finance_costs are not split in the P&L (only a net 'Net Finance Income/(Cost)' of (774) is shown); the split used here (Interest Income 29,612 / Interest Expense 30,567) is taken from the Statement of Cash Flows adjustments note, which nets to (955), leaving an unreconciled ~181k gap vs the P&L's stated (774) net finance cost -- likely a small forex/bank-charges item not separately broken out. No column-swap ambiguity was found for this filing: EPS (68,483/500,000,000=0.137 ~= stated 0.14; prior 109,252/500,000,000=0.219 ~= stated 0.22) and the Statement of Changes in Equity (Balance as at 30 June 2025 transition row shows Net Profit for the Period 109,252, matching the P&L's stated prior-year comparative) both confirm the P&L's own column order is correct as printed.

interim_updates.note_text: AGPL's Group revenue fell 15.3% YoY to Rs.1,751.3Mn (Q1 FY25/26: Rs.2,068.6Mn), driven by the Tea segment (Rs.1,736.8Mn vs Rs.2,046.9Mn, -15.1%) as sales volumes dropped 0.4Mn Kg -- management attributes this to the geopolitical situation in the Middle East depressing offtake -- even though the Net Sale Average improved by Rs.94/Kg. Hydropower (Waverly Power) revenue also fell, from Rs.21.7Mn to Rs.14.5Mn (-33.0%), and its PBT contribution declined from Rs.13.3Mn to Rs.11.8Mn (-11.6%), while Tea's PBT held up better, Rs.100.8Mn to Rs.97.7Mn (-3.1%), helped by a sharp reduction in net finance cost (Group: Rs.6.7Mn to Rs.0.8Mn) from restructuring borrowing facilities onto lower rates. Group PBT was therefore fairly resilient, down only 4.1% to Rs.109.4Mn, but PAT fell much harder, -37.3% to Rs.68.5Mn, because the Tea segment's tax expense jumped from nil to Rs.37.2Mn (the segmental note shows the prior year had a tax credit/nil charge for Tea, versus a full Rs.37.2Mn charge this year) -- so the headline PBT stability masks a much weaker post-tax outcome. Working capital moved unfavourably: inventories rose from Rs.852.3Mn to Rs.1,372.0Mn since 31 March 2026 (a Rs.519.7Mn build reflected in the Rs.75.4Mn net operating cash outflow for the quarter, versus a Rs.100.5Mn inflow a year earlier), while trade and other payables also rose (Rs.912.3Mn to Rs.1,156.0Mn) partially offsetting it.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one has been collected for AGPL -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. Balance-sheet YoY (30 June 2025 vs 30 June 2026) is also not available: the filing's Statement of Financial Position only compares the current quarter-end to the prior fiscal year-end (31 March 2026), per LKAS 34 convention, not to the same quarter a year ago -- so all balance-sheet figures stored here are point-in-time as at 30 June 2026 only, with no prior comparative stored in this row. Finance income/finance costs are estimates split from the Statement of Cash Flows interest adjustments (the P&L itself only discloses a single net 'Net Finance Income/(Cost)' line); for the Group basis this split leaves a small ~Rs.181k unreconciled gap vs the P&L's stated net figure, likely a minor forex/bank-charges item not separately disclosed -- see notes field on the GROUP financial_statements row for detail.
interim_updates.takeaway: PBT looks only modestly down (-4.1% YoY) but that's flattered by a large drop in net finance cost from debt restructuring; the more telling number is PAT (-37.3%), driven almost entirely by the Tea segment swinging from a near-nil tax charge last year to Rs.37.2Mn this year, and by a large seasonal inventory build that pushed operating cash flow negative for the quarter.
operational_highlights: Group revenue Rs.1,751.3Mn, down 15.3% YoY (Tea -15.1% to Rs.1,736.8Mn; Hydropower -33.0% to Rs.14.5Mn).
Group PBT Rs.109.4Mn (-4.1% YoY), helped by net finance cost falling from Rs.6.7Mn to Rs.0.8Mn on lower-rate refinancing.
Group PAT Rs.68.5Mn (-37.3% YoY) as Tax Expense jumped to Rs.40.9Mn from Rs.4.9Mn, mainly a Rs.37.2Mn Tea-segment charge (vs ~nil prior year).
Basic EPS fell to Rs.0.14 from Rs.0.22 (-36.4%).
Net operating cash flow was -Rs.75.4Mn (vs +Rs.100.5Mn a year earlier) due to a Rs.519.7Mn inventory build since 31 March 2026.
Net Assets per share rose to Rs.8.38 (Group) from Rs.8.24 at 31 March 2026; current ratio 1.34.
key_drivers: Tea segment volumes down 0.4Mn Kg YoY on Middle East geopolitical disruption to demand, partly offset by a Rs.94/Kg improvement in Net Sale Average.
Tea segment tax expense swung from ~nil in Q1 FY25/26 to Rs.37.2Mn in Q1 FY26/27, the single largest driver of the PAT decline.
Net finance cost (Group) fell from Rs.6.7Mn to Rs.0.8Mn on restructuring of borrowing facilities at lower interest rates.
Hydropower subsidiary (Waverly Power) revenue and PBT both fell roughly a third YoY, a smaller absolute drag but the segment with the largest percentage decline.
